articles.title: Spate of Odd Cyber-Outages Strikes US as Nations Worldwide Warn of “Mystery” Threat
articles.content:
Something eerie is afoot.
For the past few weeks, Western countries have begun playing up some unknown disaster or “event”, with UK in particular issuing breathless warnings to its citizens to stockpile goods and make emergency plans in case of some mysterious “disruptions”:
The BBC called it the coming “Black Sky” event:
"We are nine meals from anarchy" is a phrase often heard in the civil contingency world. A brutal reminder of the fear that three days without food would be enough to turn a crisis into chaos. If a Black Sky event takes out electricity, water, shops and communications, there is a good reason the government wants us to have our own supplies.
The BBC author plays up the threat by claiming he already experienced a dark “omen” even whilst writing the above article:
While writing this piece last Saturday I had to break off for an hour because my street was suddenly plunged into darkness. We had a power cut.
I found my emergency torch, but the batteries had leaked. My candles had been pushed to the back of a cupboard and I had no idea where I had put my wind-up radio with its emergency torch.
It felt like an omen.
One would assume such warnings are related to psyops about some Russian attack, but this seems different. Reading between the lines, we infer that TPTB are pushing some kind of nationwide power outage perhaps by way of “cyber attack” whom they can blame on a convenient actor for the purpose of pushing through a much darker and broader agenda.
This campaign has likewise accelerated in the US, where the FBI has warned of some unknown attacks against municipal water systems.
In the meantime, major and historic disruptions have occurred over the past few months. These include the Hugging Face incident, where OpenAI agents broke out of their containment and spread through the internet, followed by the recent widespread Microsoft outages.
Two days ago—on the ominous date of Friday the 13th—the US suddenly experienced an unprecedented nationwide disruption to the FAA flight systems, which caused the issuance of a ground stop to all flights in the country.
After some mealymouthed responses regarding the nature of the disruptions, US authorities finally claimed the issue was caused by “old equipment” at FAA sites:
Just watch the video above. Following the saga, the weirdly equivocating responses from authorities were not very reassuring, or believable for that matter. It made it easy to conclude that something is being hidden—though perhaps it is only embarrassment.
Many suspected a coverup for an Iranian attack, while conspiracy theorists naturally assumed this was either a practice run to some major cyber false flag, or perhaps the consequences of an ongoing AI containment incident. Many now believe in the wake of the Hugging Face incident, some super intelligent AIs have escaped, cloned themselves on the internet, and are proceeding to compromise and disrupt various security systems worldwide.
The Secretary of the DHS even seemed to indirectly admit that this was a possibility:
Granted, we must not forget the eternal Hanlon’s Law: “Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.”
And there is plenty of that—or at least incompetence and obsolescence—when it comes to the US power grid and general infrastructure. Shockingly, it was revealed that the FAA still runs floppy disks on much of its critical “computer” system networks:
WASHINGTON, Nov 5 (Reuters) - The US Federal Aviation Administration said on Thursday it will replace by the end of 2028 the outdated floppy disks used for weather and other critical information at more than 400 air traffic control facilities across the country.
The Enterprise Information Display System will replace four systems dating back to the 1980s and will put important operational information in one place so controllers can quickly see air traffic updates.
It’s certainly believable that simple incompetence can be at fault. But the preponderance of related odd events in sequence over the past few months is rather suspicious.
If that weren’t enough, the Pentagon launched what was being billed as a “doomsday plan” called Fortress America, an initiative for making US military bases self-sufficient in the event of some mass power grid failure:
Why the need for all these preparations all of the sudden?
Now the Mossad has reportedly warned the US that Iran is planning some major “attack” on American leaders, allegedly causing some officials to be transferred to secure facilities:
Barak Ravid of Axios—who knows a thing or two about the Mossad—not surprisingly reveals that the Mossad chief is currently in Washington to help deliver Netanyahu’s urgent pleas to resume the war with Iran:
Why it matters: The visit by Roman Gofman, one of Benjamin Netanyahu’s closest confidants, comes as the Israeli prime minister is pressing President Trump to resume the war against Iran.
Driving the news: Gofman is meeting with CIA Director John Ratcliffe, the sources said. He is also expected to travel to Miami to meet White House envoy Steve Witkoff, one of the sources said.
Surprise, surprise. Can we all see how the threads are tying together?
It’s not a far stretch to hypothesize that some of the recent psyops, false flags, and played up “threats” may be designed to further goad the US into finishing off Iran. But given the similar warnings in Europe, there is a feeling that something bigger is at play.
We know that for a long time the WEF-aligned elites had planned for another COVID-style lockdown, this time from an unnamed “cyber” threat:
It’s hard to parse between the various interwoven threads, but it’s clear there are major incentives for the elites to push these new cyber threats for a variety of related purposes. A populace in fear is one easy to browbeat into accepting hard-to-swallow consequences. On the lower end of the scale, it’s obvious that Israel may seek to stage a false flag to blame on Iran to tip Trump into finishing off its arch nemesis. On the higher end of the scale, the elites appear to be preparing to use the opportunity created by AI cyber threats to continue pushing their 2030 agenda of global centralization. Somewhere in that muddle is the genuine case of US infrastructure creaking along, one last straw away from imploding.
So, what do you make of it?

articles.title: Russian Peace Terms Reportedly Revealed, as Ukraine Again Uses Baltic Airspace to Strike St. Petersburg
articles.content:
After the trilateral meeting between representatives of Ukraine, Russia, and the US, the Kushner-Witkoff team traveled to Moscow to deliver their messages directly to Putin himself.
One of the most interesting revelations from this meeting surround Russia’s alleged demands for the new “European security architecture” that would reset Russia’s relations with the West and end the war in Ukraine. According to BILD and other rumor mills, Russia’s demands for the full security reset were heard for the first time:
They allegedly include the following:
A NEW SECURITY ARCHITECTURE?
Bild published an article claiming to list Russia’s supposed demands and proposals for restructuring the security architecture in Europe.
According to the publication, Russia demands:
* Finland’s withdrawal from NATO;
* Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania must refuse to host NATO military bases;
* Ukraine must renounce its membership in NATO, cede all of Donbas to Russia, and recognize Russia’s control over the remaining occupied territories. Membership in the EU is permissible;
* Odessa and Mykolaiv must be demilitarized and cannot be used as naval bases;
* Moldova must become a federation that includes Transnistria and Gagauzia. If the country joins the EU, these regions will be able to hold referendums on independence.
In turn, Moscow is allegedly ready to offer to withdraw nuclear weapons and intermediate-range missiles from Belarus, as well as to withdraw Russian troops from Transnistria.
Officially, of course, no one has made such statements. And the list seems somewhat... naive, to say the least. So, for now, this is all just the authors’ speculation.
The above sounds reasonable, if true. Russia’s concessions are not major: The withdrawal of nuclear missiles from Belarus is nothing—Russia does not need to station them there to be able to threaten Europe, or anyone else for that matter. The rest of Russia’s demands should not be difficult for the West to implement, were it to actually desire peace in Ukraine. But knowing London’s and Brussel’s thirst for war, we can conclude that there is little chance they’d agree to the humiliating back-pedal of being forced to boot Finland back out of NATO, amongst other things. That said, as the pain gets sharper and sharper for Europe and Ukraine, eventually these terms will likely begin looking far more attractive, and thus we can conclude these are fairly realistic and healthy terms for the war to be concluded on.
That said, this only pertains to terms vis-a-vis Europe. This does not even begin accounting for Russia’s previously stated demands for Ukraine itself: those of demilitarization, deNazification, etc. Thus, it’s likely a long road still ahead, but this feels like the first semi-realistic proposal which could actually lead to an eventual conclusion to the war; in short, a good and honest starting foundation for settlement.
By far the most important point left out by the above summary, however, was Putin’s direct demand that no foreign troops can be allowed on Ukrainian soil in the post-settlement phase. Putin stated this directly to Witkoff-Kushner in the public portion of the face-off:
Listen carefully to Putin’s words at the end when he says that the presence of European troops in Ukraine would mean the immediate resumption of the war.
This comes just days after British publications boasted that British troops would be allowed to shoot back at the Russians once they deploy to Ukraine:
It’s easy to see why Putin would be concerned.
The other thing that’s easy to see is that Europe will not be able to swallow its pride in accepting any of these demands any time soon, and so there is virtually no chance any kind of peace can be found any time soon.
The only guaranteed trajectory is one toward more escalation. And that came two days ago on November 11 during what was called the largest Ukrainian attack on the Russian Leningrad region since the start of the war. The strikes again featured Ukrainian drones flying through NATO’s Baltic airspace, as admitted to directly by the Estonian MFA:
A plethora of official reports from both Lithuania and Latvia also confirmed drones again crossing their airspaces:
They again blamed Russian EW:
An unidentified flying object, believed to be a drone, crossed Lithuanian airspace overnight into Wednesday. Minister of National Defence Robertas Kaunas says the unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) may have been knocked off course by Russian electronic warfare measures.
Fighter jets conducting the NATO Baltic Air Policing Mission attempted to neutralise the UAV. "According to the Lithuanian Armed Forces and the Air Force, an air defence mission was underway. There was one unidentified object flying in Lithuanian airspace, most likely a drone. All the parameters suggest it was a drone, and an attempt was made to neutralise it," the minister told LRT Television on Wednesday.
Reuters reported:
VILNIUS, Nov 11 (Reuters) - NATO scrambled jets overnight after at least four drones strayed into the airspace of the Baltic states during Ukrainian strikes on Russia, officials said on Wednesday, triggering brief alerts to citizens of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to seek shelter.
Ukrainian military drones straying into the airspace of Finland and the Baltics this year have fuelled concern that the Ukraine war is spilling into NATO countries that border Russia and its ally Belarus.
We can at this point conclude that there is no question Ukraine is deliberately utilizing NATO airspace to attack Russian regions. Multiple such incidents in a row could not possibly be explained by sheer “coincidence” or chance of some sort any longer. The only question that remains is what precise flight path is Ukraine utilizing.
The clues from the new attack are as follows. The above Reuters piece states that alerts were issued in the central city of Kaunas, Lithuania and that “Two attempts were made to shoot down a drone over Lithuania but both failed, and it later crossed into neighbouring Latvia's airspace, Lithuanian armed forces Chief of Defence Staff Giedrius Premeneckas told a news conference.”
If the drone alert was around Kaunas and “later crossed into neighboring Latvia”, that means the flight path can only have been as follows:
This leaves us to again assume the drones are either going through Poland, or being launched from Poland itself.
Another article from a Lithuanian paper bizarrely states that one of the drones appeared to have come from Belarus, while another crossed Polish territory near the Suwalki Gap and then turned toward Lithuania:
"According to the Lithuanian Armed Forces and the Air Force, an air defence mission was underway. There was one unidentified object flying in Lithuanian airspace, most likely a drone. All the parameters suggest it was a drone, and an attempt was made to neutralise it," the minister told LRT Television on Wednesday.
According to Kaunas, the Lithuanian military received information from Belarus about unidentified objects at 10:47 pm on Tuesday. The information was relayed through a technical communication channel that Belarus periodically uses to notify Lithuania of objects flying towards its territory. The minister said some of the objects initially detected never reached Lithuanian airspace, instead turning towards Latvia and Russia. One object entered Lithuanian airspace from Belarus at around 11 pm. According to the defence minister, it remained in Lithuanian airspace for about five minutes, crossed the Polish border area towards the Suwałki Gap and later turned back across Lithuanian territory.
The article further states that balloons were likewise detected over Baltic airspace:
Smuggler balloons were detected as well The defence minister also confirmed that the overnight incidents were not limited to airspace violations, with balloons were also detected flying over the region. Balloon activity temporarily disrupted operations at Vilnius and Kaunas airports.
This is particularly noteworthy because after a Russian Air Force colonel was reportedly assassinated in St. Petersburg at the same time, reports indicated that the bomb used for the attack was delivered to Russia by a “hot air balloon flying from the Baltic countries”:
Ukraine delivering objects, including drones, to Russia via balloon has become a common occurrence, as seen here in a Russian drone intercept video:
It should be noted that the Estonian Defense Minister on the other hand claimed that the drones which violated Estonian airspace came from the east of the country, i.e. the Russian direction, rather than from the other Baltics by way of Poland:
Minister of Defense Martin Herem said Ukraine’s attack on Ust-Luga began around midnight and continued until approximately 6 a.m. Wednesday. Most of the drones flew close to Estonia’s border but remained in Russian airspace.
At around 3:30 a.m., one drone briefly entered Estonian airspace from the direction of Latvia before continuing toward Russia. Several drones that reached Ust-Luga subsequently turned west and circled over the Gulf of Finland in Russian airspace. Some briefly crossed into Estonian airspace over the gulf.
The reason for utilizing such a “border-skirting” technique is clear. The article states that Russia does not shoot down the drones which are just outside of its own territory:
"If it's very close to the border and Russia is on the other side, shooting it down isn't sensible either. Incidentally, Russia does exactly the same thing: Near its own border, it only engages drones when it can fire toward its own territory."
Knowing such rules of engagement, Ukraine is likely using the border-skirting tactic in order to keep the drones from being shot down as they traverse toward their target. This would explain how and why the drones are able to reach the St. Petersburg region from Ukrainian territory without being shot down.
But clearly, it appears Ukraine is utilizing both flight paths, the above and through Poland and the Baltics, and perhaps even Belarus, as well.
Despite all this, Ukraine is now experiencing renewed issues. As some Ukrainian officers predicted last month, the Starlink/Starshield throttling has returned, again critically crippling Ukrainian drone capabilities:
At this point it’s next to impossible to guess why these games are being played off and on. If I had to guess, I would say when media attention put the issue in the spotlight, political pressure forced whoever was responsible behind the scenes to turn the Starlink back on. Now that the spotlight has worn off, the same people perhaps decided it’s safe to turn it back off without incurring further pressure.
Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee Gregory Meeks took notice and issued an immediate statement:
We can only further assume that pressure is building behind the scenes to force Zelensky into accepting the latest US proposals to end the war, with coercive “arm-twisting” tactics now being applied.
—
While Ukraine’s Starshield experiences renewed throttling, a new update has brought news that Russian Geran drones are now being found with Bureau 1440 terminals attached:
You’ll recall last time a Russian Molniya drone with a Rassvet terminal was found, this time it was a Geran drone.
A Russian military channel reports:
Russia is reportedly beginning tests of “Geran-2” loitering munitions equipped with terminals from the domestic satellite communication system “Rassvet,” developed by the “Bureau 1440” company.
This involves the potential integration of a satellite communication channel directly into the drone’s onboard equipment. This would allow the transmission of video and telemetry data to the operator, as well as the reception of control commands from a significantly greater distance than from ground communication stations.
The main difference between this configuration and a standard “Geran-2” is the ability to maintain two-way communication during flight. Instead of simply following a pre-programmed route, the drone could potentially receive updated commands and transmit information from its onboard cameras to the operator.
This expands the capabilities for reconnaissance, surveillance, and flight task adjustments, while simultaneously reducing reliance on ground repeaters.
In 2026, Russia launched 32 “Rassvet-3” satellites into orbit in two batches of 16 each. As of early November, 30 satellites remained in orbit.
The current size of the constellation allows for communication only during specific periods when the satellites pass over Ukrainian territory. According to estimates by Ukrainian experts, this amounts to at least two extended communication sessions per day.
Therefore, the potential equipping of “Geran” drones with “Rassvet” terminals represents one of the first applications of the Russian low-orbit satellite constellation for military purposes.
As the number of satellites increases, the system could potentially provide more sustained communication with drones, approaching the operational principles of the American Starlink.
In Ukraine, the Starshield system continues to slow down.
This was reported by Zelensky in his channel.
According to the head of the Kiеv regime, speed restrictions on the Starshield system, at a level of 161 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour), have been in effect along the entire front line for several days.
According to him, Ukrainian military personnel have already investigated the situation and determined that this is a systemic speed limitation.
Lastly, a poll:
What do you think about the latest claimed peace terms offered by Russia, which include Finland out of NATO, Donbass to Russia, no European troops in Ukraine, no NATO military bases in Baltic states, Odessa and Nikolayev to become demilitarized, and Moldova to become a federation?

articles.title: War of Paradoxes: Abu Dhabi Negotiations Highlight Ukraine Conflict’s Increasing Informational Divergence
articles.content:
Delegations from Russia, Ukraine, and the US met in Adu Dhabi for a new trilateral negotiations attempt billed as bringing the war one step closer to its end. The meeting was notably attended by higher ranking representatives than usual, such as Kyrylo Budanov on the Ukrainian side and Putin aide Medinsky for the Russians, while being hosted by Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff.
The results of the meeting showed the Russian and Ukrainian positions as divided as usual, in fact more so. The Russian side has continued to demand total capitulation of the Donbass territories, while Ukraine is now adamant that no territory can be ceded. In a “twist” tactic, the US attempted to propose a redrawing of Donbass boundaries so that Russia could announce “victory” without having to capture the remaining physical territory. This was apparently rejected by both sides, and the deadlock remained.
There is no possibility of a territorial exchange between Russia and Ukraine, stated Vladimir Medinsky, head of the Russian negotiating group in Abu Dhabi, in an interview with the "Vesti" news agency.
According to him, the main goal of the negotiations is to create a new security system in Europe, which will become the new "Yalta" and "Potsdam."
Medinsky also stated that Russia will be satisfied with the results of the negotiations when peace is achieved on its terms.
Leaving little to interpretation, Medinsky went on to succinctly clarify that Russia intends to return “every inch” of land that it feels belongs to it:
One of the sly new tricks the US-Ukrainian side is attempting to impose on Russia is a kind of escalatory armistice regime that is meant to gradually “warm” Russia to a progressively expanding set of ceasefires. The purpose here is clearly to set new precedents with each small ceasefire, while slowly goading Russia into what the US hopes will eventually become a permanent armistice across the entire front—a kind of boiling frog strategy toward sneakily ending the conflict:
According to unconfirmed information—specifically, snippets and leaks emerging from Abu Dhabi—the Ukrainian side has proposed a "freeze" along the entire Kherson/Dnieper sector of the line of contact. As a starting point, they are using their recent incursion into Russian-held territory near the settlement of Oleshky in the Kherson region as a basis for this proposal.
They are also suggesting the declaration of an extended "Christmas truce."
Included in this same package is the now-"traditional" proposal for a maritime and energy-related ceasefire.
Perhaps this is the very reason why Witkoff and Kushner are departing for Moscow in a few hours—to persuade the Russians to embrace "humanitarianism." Will there be anyone in the Kremlin foolish enough to grant Ukraine a winter respite?
First, it started with Melania Trump’s recent ceasefire in Oleshky, in the Kherson region. Now they hope to expand that toward more frequent holiday-based ceasefires, wider ceasefires along the entire Dnieper front, Black Sea corridor ceasefires, then eventually a winter-long ceasefire across the entire frontline. The purpose is to eventually coax Russia, in very gradual fashion, into halting all operations.
Lavrov commented on the talks, very keenly understanding that the West wants to “rush” Russia into halting military action before reaching any true agreements:
His point: Russia seeks an agreement on a wide-scale and new pan-European security architecture first, then a ceasefire after that. Brussels, on the other hand, demands an immediate ceasefire and only then will allow discussion of security agreements.
One of the fascinating quirks of the negotiations that continues to demonstrate the conflict’s internecine nature: One of Ukraine’s main negotiators was born in Sochi, Russia; while both of Russia’s main negotiators were born in Ukraine—Medinsky in the city of Smila near the Dnieper river, and Dmitriev in Kiev:
Then there’s the recent revelation that top Ukrainian presidential advisor Mykhailo Podolyak’s brother Vladimir Podolyak was killed on the frontline while fighting for Russia:
It proves the conflict is much closer to a civil war than anything else, when you really think about it.
But the other more salient revelation from the negotiations is how epistemologically divergent the conflict has become. Zelensky highlighted this fact when he explained how the Russian side believes itself to control all of Donbass, when in fact Ukrainian soldiers are present in large areas of it:
In recent months, both the Ukrainian and Russian sides have utilized AI showing soldiers capturing areas that they did not actually capture. The evolution of “slow-trickle” and dispersion tactics has also created a situation where no one seems to know or agree on who exactly controls what anymore along the front. Top map-makers on both sides have now diverged more than ever before, to the point that understanding the situation of control on the ground is now beholden more to faithful adherence to one side’s “gospel” over the other.
A large part of this issue can arguably be attributed to different definitions of what “control” represents. For instance, some on the Ukrainian side have accused Russia of considering any area to have been infiltrated even by a lone soldier to be under its nominal “control”. The Ukrainian side rejects this definition, and believes control should only be defined by more rigorous standards. Much of the frontline has now devolved into an unprecedented point of no return where “control” becomes a matter of opinion and orientation of one’s loyalties. This is best illustrated by the following post, which indicates Russian and Ukrainian positions intermixed amongst each other in and around Konstantinovka:

articles.title: Relentless Russian Strikes Knock Out Kiev’s Power, as Iskander Missile Gouges Capital City’s North Bridge
articles.content:
Last night Russia hit Kiev’s North Bridge with an Iskander missile. Only one strike has been fully visually confirmed, but there were again rumored to be several that potentially hit.
If you’ll recall, the North Bridge was first hit in an experimental fashion with some form of Geran drone on October 3, which caused the following damage:
Then, after hitting the South Bridge cable stays with a “wire-cutter” drone, Russia proceeded to hit it again with an Iskander last week, creating a major crater in the middle of it:
Incidentally, we’ve also now obtained a new photo of the damage from this attack, seen from below the South Bridge:
Now, Iskanders have targeted the key North Bridge, which is Kiev’s most important and highest-trafficked of its six major road bridges. The damage can be seen in the report below:
The accuracy was once more pinpoint.
One theory suggested that Russia was attempting to target the anchor point of the giant cable stays:
It would make sense, given Russia’s previous attempts to hit the South Bridge’s cables via the new specialized “wire-cutter” drones earlier last month.
Top Ukrainian expert Serhiy “Flash” Beskrestnov writes of the Iskander’s accuracy:
Unfortunately, the enemy is very accurately targeting bridges. How is this possible?
Under conditions of complete navigation suppression across the entire country during air raid alerts, it is difficult for the "Iskander" missile to hit a target with meter-level accuracy. An inertial system alone cannot provide that level of precision.
However, our enemy wants to hit its targets. Therefore, "Iskander" missiles use optical guidance heads (9Э436, 9Б918) or expensive radar-guided heads (9Б918).
During the descent of the warhead, a radar scan of the area takes place over a few seconds, and a correction is entered into the missile's guidance system.
He provided interesting links to two recovered components of the Russian Iskander, showing a radar homing head, and an optical “matching” unit, presumably akin to a DSMAC (Digital Scene Matching Area Correlator) system:
The DSMAC would compare the visual of the target with images of the same target stored in its memory in order to much more precisely hit the exact area that’s needed to be hit, rather than relying simply on GPS/Glonass, which can be degraded via spoofing and jamming.
This could explain why some Iskanders have at times appeared inaccurate. Russia may use the cheaper variants without these homing heads when needing to hit something large or not particularly important. Other times when absolute accuracy is necessary, it can use the variants loaded with the above more expensive and advanced homing units.
What we can conclude for now is that Russia’s debridgification campaign is certainly proceeding in a more systematic fashion than ever before. But the Russian leadership does not appear in a particular hurry to try and disable the bridge entirely and all at once.
It’s clear that the Iskander’s accuracy is allowing it to hit fairly the bridge roadway accurately without major misses, and so it’s conceivable that Russia could easily smash the bridge with a barrage of simultaneous Iskanders. But for now it appears Russia is happy to peck at it incrementally. One of the only logical explanation is one we gave last time: Russia could be deliberately aiming to tie up as much of Ukraine’s civil resources as possible, dragging out the repair work to strain the state to the breaking point.
It’s conceivable that Russia may even not seek to bring the bridge down entirely, but rather simply make it unusable for now. This would be the case if the MOD envisions capturing Kiev later and needing the bridges to be in a semi-restorable state.
There’s also a non-zero chance that the Russian MOD is just shooting from the hip with no real plan, merely hitting things probingly on a whim and hoping for “something” to happen. After all, one could easily come to such a conclusion after seeing the repeated strikes carried out against the Zatoka bridge in Odessa, amongst others.
The campaign comes amid rumors that Putin has privately relayed to Ukraine he intends to destroy all Ukraine’s infrastructure by next year if Ukraine refuses to capitulate:
The FT article in question writes:
The Russian president views his air strikes as retaliation for Ukraine’s drone attacks on refineries and commercial warehouses in Russia this summer and blames Kyiv for the collapse of previous ceasefires, according to another person.
“I will destroy all your infrastructure until you agree,” the second person said, relaying Putin’s position. “By next year Ukraine won’t have any infrastructure left. All the bridges, ports, railways, energy infrastructure, power stations . . . will have been destroyed.”
Zelensky himself appeared to indirectly corroborate it by announcing that Russia is preparing even more large infrastructure strikes:
Though we are of course to be suspicious of any MSM “leaks” of this sort, the truth is that:
Previous such leaks turned out to be true. We reported several months ago rumors that Russia was getting ready to disable Kiev’s bridges. This appeared to prove exceedingly accurate.
It would positively explain why Europe and the US have gone absolutely hysterical with ceasefire attempts, showing urgency to end the war like never before. We can only assume this has to do with the fact that they know they are unable to save Ukraine from what is “coming soon”.
All this past week, Russia has been striking Ukrainian power plants, here the Dniprovska Thermal Power Plant in Dnipropetrovsk seen being hit by cruise missiles on November 3rd:
The strikes were extensive:
The Russian army continues to systematically disable Ukraine’s energy and infrastructure.
▪️Last night, Russian troops launched a massive strike with high-precision weapons and attack drones against Ukraine’s energy and port infrastructure.
➖Ladzhyinskaya Thermal Power Plant - 1800 MW.
➖Kryvorozhskaya Thermal Power Plant - 2800 MW.
➖Prydneprovskaya Thermal Power Plant - 1765 MW.
➖Kharkov Thermal Power Plant - 86 MW.
➖”Zmiivska” substation - 330 kV.
➖”Losevo” substation - 330 kV.
▪️In the Odesa region, the port infrastructure in the port of Kiliya, used in the interests of the Ukrainian Armed Forces, was hit. In the port of Yuzhny and the Black Sea, two dry cargo ships carrying military equipment and dual-use cargo for the Ukrainian Armed Forces were hit.
▪️The targets of the strikes were facilities that ensure the energy supply to the Ukrainian military industry and the Ukrainian Armed Forces, as well as military logistics through the Black Sea ports.
The attacks reportedly triggered the “most severe water outage” of the war for Kiev:
A Ukrainian energy expert says that the grid will never return to its previous levels:
Ukraine’s energy system will not return to its previous capacity.
▪️ Ukrainian energy expert Yuriy Korolchuk stated that it will no longer be possible to restore the country’s energy system to its previous level.
▪️ According to him, the third power distribution scheme created since the beginning of the conflict has been destroyed by strikes. The previous ones were developed in 2022 and 2024, and the latest one in 2026.
▪️ Korolchuk emphasized that damage to energy facilities in Kyiv, Kharkiv, Dnipro, and Odesa is affecting even the western regions of Ukraine, as the entire country is connected by a single energy system.
Here the Director for the Center of Ukraine’s Energy Research Alexander Kharchenko states that all three of Kiev’s main power plants are effectively destroyed:
Director for the center of Ukraine's energy research, Alexander Kharchenko, reports that the 3 main Power Plants in the city of Kyiv have been completely destroyed.
CHP-4, CHP-5, CHP-6, have lost basically all of there energy generation capacity. He states that less than 15% of equipment at these facilities can be repaired.
He also warned that outages in Kyiv may last for up to 36 hours at a time.
—
Now the latest developments continue to revolve around the issue of Starlink and its Russian analogue over Ukraine.
Firstly, Ukrainian expert Serhiy Flash reports that Russians are jamming Ukraine’s own Starlinks with increasing effectiveness. They are doing this by both multiplying the number of new “Volna Kupol Garant” jammers, as well as making them more compact in size. He claims Russia has covered almost all of Crimea with these systems already, which could explain the lack of Starlink-drone attacks on Crimea in recent months. Now it is beginning to fill the battlefield with them:
Our adversary continues to increase the number of satellite electronic warfare (EW) systems that interfere with the operation of Starlink. The system operates on the principle of area coverage, protecting an area of approximately 25 square kilometers. The Russians have deployed this type of EW system to protect almost all important facilities in Crimea and are increasingly using it along the front line.
The days when this EW complex looked like 6 trailers parked next to each other in a single location are long gone. Now, the enemy is trying to camouflage it. The core of the complex consists of satellite direct-focus antennas with a diameter of approximately one meter. Regardless of the camouflage used, they must have a clear line of sight (without obstructions) in the zenith, which limits the possibilities for camouflage.
My colleagues from aerial reconnaissance constantly ask me where to look and what to look for.
Pay attention to truck parking areas – these are ideal places for camouflaging the complex. Out of dozens of trucks, 3-6 may have the system installed. Also, pay attention to small trailers attached to cars. The enemy has devised a method of installing one antenna (instead of two) in small trailers that are parked close together but spread out across the area.
Camouflage netting in the rear is likely to attract attention, so its use is unlikely. The EW system can operate under a polycarbonate awning or under a plastic sheet. Pay attention to opaque greenhouses.
Many people write about the enormous power consumption and the need to install the complex near power substations. This is not the case. The complex can even operate on generators.
The EW system operates in the frequency range of 14.0–14.5 GHz.
At the same time, Russia has accelerated development of its own Rassvet (“Dawn”) analogue, and mainstream medias are growing concerned:
Reuters reports that Russia is planning to send up more of them by the end of 2026, and that Ukraine’s GUR confirms Russia is already actively using the satellites for military purposes over Ukraine:
Moscow plans further Rassvet launches by the end of 2026 to increase the network’s geographic coverage, bringing it gradually closer to a full low-orbit satellite communications system, GUR said in a written statement.
“Russia is using the ‘Rassvet’ satellite system over the territory of Ukraine for military purposes,” GUR spokesman Andrii Yusov said in the statement.
This comes amid reports that Russia has already begun registering the newest, most advanced variant called the Rassvet-4, which appeared in the registry on October 29th:
Applications for the registration of the Rassvet-4 satellite network, which involves the deployment of 374 spacecraft, have appeared in the International Telecommunication Union’s database.
This is evidenced by documents from the International Telecommunication Union (ITU).
According to the published data, the applications were entered into the registry on October 29, 2026.
The proposed constellation is to consist of 374 satellites placed at an altitude of approximately 800 km. They are planned to be distributed across 17 orbital planes—22 satellites in each.
Just as those reports hit the airwaves, Russia made another successful launch of the Soyuz-2.1b carrying some unknown military cargo which some suspect to have been Rassvet satellites, perhaps even of the new Rassvet-4 variety:
Serhiy Flash himself urged that up to 20 Rassvet satellites could have been amongst the cargo:
As we have written here many times, next year bodes extremely badly for Ukraine given the confluence of factors:
Ukraine’s own Starlink is being increasingly jammed and made ineffective
Russia’s Starlink analogue is becoming increasingly operational, while Ukraine will never have the capability to jam it the way Russia jams Ukraine’s Starlink
Russia is slowly covering all of its refineries with large defensive structures, from layered metal grid-works to nets
The third point above alone will eventually take away Ukraine’s only trump card, leaving Zelensky with little leverage. At the same time, Russia’s own growing Rassvet trump card will come to impose increasingly severe costs on the Ukrainian state, as Russia will be able to target everything in the “rear” that was hitherto relatively safe.
2027 will likely be an extremely incoherent year, at least for those not tuned in to the truly fine details of the conflict. The frontline may continue to appear regressed while Russia will build an unprecedentedly widening disparity in capabilities which will leave observers confused as to “who is winning”. But it will be akin to watching two opponents in a knife fight, one of which has severe internal bleeding that is not visible to the naked eye. To many, the fight will appear “even” for a while—until it doesn’t.
That said, the war may go on for quite a while longer given Russia’s increasingly comfortable position, which will likely grow even more comfortable after the refineries are made safe from drone attacks. Once the Rassvet system is fully operational and integrated, and the Ukrainian state is even more economically and politically depleted, Russia could choose to tighten the noose and launch far larger ground operations as a final deathblow phase.

▪️Last night, Russian troops launched a massive strike with high-precision weapons and attack drones against Ukraine’s energy and port infrastructure.
➖Ladzhyinskaya Thermal Power Plant - 1800 MW.

➖Prydneprovskaya Thermal Power Plant - 1765 MW.
➖Kharkov Thermal Power Plant - 86 MW.

➖”Losevo” substation - 330 kV.

The attacks reportedly triggered the “most severe water outage” of the war for Kiev:

Ukraine’s energy system will not return to its previous capacity.

▪️ According to him, the third power distribution scheme created since the beginning of the conflict has been destroyed by strikes. The previous ones were developed in 2022 and 2024, and the latest one in 2026.

  3. Russia is slowly covering all of its refineries with large defensive structures, from layered metal grid-works to nets

At the same time, Russia’s own growing Rassvet trump card will come to impose increasingly severe costs on the Ukrainian state, as Russia will be able to target everything in the “rear” that was hitherto relatively safe.

2027 will likely be an extremely incoherent year, at least for those not tuned in to the truly fine details of the conflict. The frontline may continue to appear regressed while Russia will build an unprecedentedly widening disparity in capabilities which will leave observers confused as to “who is winning”. But it will be akin to watching two opponents in a knife fight, one of which has severe internal bleeding that is not visible to the naked eye. To many, the fight will appear “even” for a while—until it doesn’t.

That said, the war may go on for quite a while longer given Russia’s increasingly comfortable position, which will likely grow even more comfortable after the refineries are made safe from drone attacks. Once the Rassvet system is fully operational and integrated, and the Ukrainian state is even more economically and politically depleted, Russia could choose to tighten the noose and launch far larger ground operations as a final deathblow phase.

articles.content:
In the aftermath of the Donald Tusk administration’s judicial coup attempt in Poland, the country has seen a spate of strange happenings.
Several Polish officials connected to the opposition have noted a distinct German flavor behind the events. We’ve seen the video of MEP Dominik Tarczynski revealing that Germany, as the main economic driver of the EU, seeks to offload some of its financial burden onto Poland, which is viewed as a kind of EU freeloader, given its pesky “sovereign” status. As such, it is in the German state’s interests to subjugate Poland and use it not only as a migrant dumping ground, but a financial boost to the struggling EU.
During the coup attempt, there were various rumors of German involvement, which included observation of German convoys on Polish highways, as well as far-right Polish figure Grzegorz Braun’s claims that the “police” surrounding the Sejm during the coup were “impostors”, with some even claiming they did not speak Polish and may have been Germans in disguise.
Most of these were subsequently debunked, though some of the “debunkings” were a little suspect—for instance, the community note for the above video dismisses it as “normal” that German police can enter Poland:
Sure, just because legal justification exists, it’s totally normal for German police to be driving around Warsaw during a major judicial coup attempt. Context matters.
Even so, many oddities yet remain.
Following the coup fiasco, over the past week German soldiers have been seen wandering around Warsaw, with various conspiratorial rumors suggesting they were being positioned as the backstop in case Tusk’s power grab turned ugly.
A video below capturing a member of the Polish parliament confronting these German troops on the street just outside the Polish parliament in Warsaw:
As the German soldier explains, Germany is attending a “coalition of the willing” exercise, along with other NATO allies, that just happens to be set in Poland.
This exercise, called Coalition 2026 and to take place between November 9th to the 22nd, is the inaugural one of its kind and is set to feature the “first [ever] military maneuver of the “Coalition of the Willing” in support of Ukraine in Poland”.
French presidential candidate Florian Philippot has twigged to the ‘convenient’ timing of these exercises:
Well, well, right in the middle of a Europeanist coup d’état, France and the United Kingdom are going to mobilize nearly 3,000 troops in POLAND in a few days to “prepare for deployment in Ukraine”!
(cf: https://lemonde.fr/international/article/2026/11/02/en-pologne-premier-exercice-militaire-grandeur-nature-pour-la-coalition-des-volontaires_6805259_3210.html)
“In Poland, first full-scale military exercise for the coalition of volunteers!”
“The ‘Koalicja’ exercise will take place in Nowa Dęba, in the southeast of the country, from November 9 to 22.
Nearly 2,800 soldiers, mostly French, are to be deployed to test this alliance’s ability to deploy in the event of a ceasefire in Ukraine!”
Euro-Atlanticist law-and-order operation!
Right in the midst of a coup attempt led by Tusk and the EU against the sovereignist and peace forces in Poland...
France has no business being there.
France must reclaim its freedom by leaving the EU and NATO, urgently!
Many conspiracies surrounding the events have abounded:
Various false flags and other secret motives are often carried out under the guise of military exercises. It is one of the quintessentially classic ways of carrying out covert transfers and staging of troops for upcoming hybrid operations. Russia itself did it multiple times, including for the seizure of Crimea and in preparation for the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, wherein a convenient set of “exercises” was carried out in Belarus that required the massing of a large number of Russian forces. Similarly, Russia often accused Ukraine of staging exercises, like the Sea Breeze in 2021, to covertly transfer weapons and position troops in preparation for war on Donbass.
It’s an age-old tactic, and as such we should not dismiss the import of German troops being present in Poland merely under the framing that they’re only there for innocent exercise reasons.
One of the clues to the more nefarious nature of these clandestine happenings is the fact that during all of this, Poland suddenly launched a “special security operation” along the Russian Kaliningrad border, citing some kind of elevated threat emergency:
Listen to Tusk’s own announcement of the situation:
What can we make of all this? At the minimum Tusk is attempting to use the well-worn tactic of deflection from his coup attempt. Any leader facing a pressing or ‘uncomfortable’ issue will always seek to deflect to some “grave danger” in need of urgent attention; hint: Trump, Epstein files, Iran.
Launching into damage control mode, Tusk is desperately trying to paper over his Brussels-led coup by conjuring imagined bogeymen at Poland’s borders. That much is certain. However, the very ‘coincidental’ involvement of NATO, and particularly German, troops on Polish soil while this is all going on makes it easy to assume other darker motives afoot among these developments. After all, in his address above, Tusk himself explains that he received some “warning” of a Russian provocation from NATO’s Supreme Allied Commander Europe, general Alexus Grynkewich; it’s not a long shot to assume these things are closely related.
It should also be said, Tusk’s panic at the notion of Russian troops lurking near the Polish border, while German troops openly march through the streets of Warsaw, is itself a comedic coup de grace.
Meanwhile, Canada reportedly stationed troops on the Russian Latvian border, again as part of some cooked-up exercises called “Resolute Reforger 2026”, which just happen to be going on at the same time:
There is too little to go on, but we can at least speculate that perhaps NATO and German troops’ presence in Poland was meant as a potential contingency for things going haywire. After all, we know that Tusk calculated the timing for the coup meticulously: He waited until the All Saints holiday, and for the Polish president to fly out of the country, not dissimilar to the August coup of 1991 when Gorbachev had left Moscow to Crimea, whereupon the coup plotters sprang on him.
Now President Nawrocki has humiliated Tusk for his attempt:
The opposition in the Sejm likewise had a message for a smugly gloating Tusk this morning:
As for the Constitutional Tribunal over which this entire conflict erupted, Tusk’s usurper Anna Korwin-Piotrowska attempted to declare a quorum with only 8 of the 15 judges in an ongoing effort to take control of the court:
This means that her coup is still in progress, with her assuming de facto control of the Tribunal after booting Tribunal president Bogdan Swieczkowski. While the opposing side now adjudges her and the Tribunal’s actions as illegitimate, the reality is that she has gained control on Tusk’s behalf and is proceeding forward slowly. That said, her order to suspend previous president Bogdan Swieczkowski is meant to last only for a month, and no one knows what will happen when that time is up. Anna Korwin-Piotrowska will attempt to indefinitely extend the order, as per the NED journal’s outlines for “transitional justice” and removal of Nawrocki’s people, which we covered last time.
Essentially, that means the coup is still in progress and is far from its decisive conclusion.
As a last relevant video, here is the German Armed Forces’ highest ranking official Christian Freuding explaining what it is that Europe is fighting for with all these efforts to push out the Russian “influence”, which includes the German political opposition:
“To give up everything for freedom, that is [true] freedom.”
You see, under the Brussels regime, the definition of freedom is giving up everything for the privilege of being ruled by the EU politburo. It turns out, slavery is actually freedom, after all—or was it the other way around?
You know where we’ve heard that one before.
